options.explanation: A ratio compares the relative sizes of two or more amounts. Their order must remain fixed because reversing the order produces a different ratio.
Treating the order as interchangeable is a common mistake. A ratio compares amounts in a fixed order, since changing the order changes the meaning of the ratio.
Subtracting amounts finds their difference, not their ratio. A ratio compares the relative sizes of amounts in a fixed order.
Ratios can sometimes be converted into percentages, but the amounts do not need to represent equal percentages. A ratio directly compares amounts in a fixed order.
